summary: Add a tamper‑evident ledger that records every receipt and mileage operation, supports history views, export verification, and backup integrity checks. Implement ledger core (src/lib/ledger.ts) with append‑only encrypted storage, canonical JSON hashing (SHA‑256 via @noble/hashes), import of existing data on first launch, and verifyLedger routine. Extend receipt and mileage stores to push ledger entries on create, update, delete. Add UI screens for History (detail view) and ledger status in Settings. Update ui_flow.json to include the new navigation steps. Ensure backup and restore incorporate ledger verification, and older backups are imported as "imported" entries. All existing tests must keep passing; new unit and acceptance tests will cover hash chaining, detection of tampering, history correctness, import behavior, export verification, and backup validation.
steps: 1. Create src/lib/ledger.ts: define LedgerEntry type, constants, helper functions for canonical JSON (stable field order), hash calculation (import { sha256 } from '@noble/hashes/sha2.js', { bytesToHex, utf8ToBytes } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js'), appendEntry(entryWithoutHash) that computes hash, sets prevHash, seq, at (ISO string), stores entry encrypted via Store.append (new method to be added). Provide methods: initLedgerIfNeeded(store) – on first launch reads existing receipts and mileage entries and writes a single imported entry per record, with import date; addEntry(kind, recordId, data) used by stores; verifyLedger(store) – reads all entries, recomputes hashes, returns {ok, entries, firstBadSeq?, reason?}. Export needed functions.

2. Extend src/lib/storage/store.ts (or create a small wrapper) with a new method appendLedgerEntry(entry: LedgerEntry): Promise<void> that reads existing ledger array (or empty), pushes new entry, writes back encrypted JSON. Ensure no overwriting of previous entries; only delete on full data reset.

3. Update src/lib/receiptStore.ts: after any successful createReceipt, editReceipt, deleteReceipt, call ledger.addEntry with kind 'receipt.created', 'receipt.corrected', or 'receipt.deleted' respectively. Pass full record content after change (for deletion, pass the last known content). Include OCR pre‑fill and user‑confirmed data in the stored data object (e.g., { ...receipt, ocrData }). Ensure the store continues to use encrypted storage as before.

4. Update src/lib/mileageStore.ts similarly: after addMileageEntry, editMileageEntry, deleteMileageEntry call ledger.addEntry with 'mileage.created', 'mileage.corrected', 'mileage.deleted'. Store full mileage record after change.

5. Modify src/lib/backup.ts: when creating a backup, include the ledger array in the backup payload under key "ledger". When restoring, first call ledger.verifyLedger on the restored payload; if verification fails, throw an error with a friendly message ("Backup verification failed – data may be tampered"). If backup has no ledger (old version), after successful restore import each receipt/mileage as 'imported' ledger entries using ledger.addEntry with kind 'imported' and the import date set to now.
6. Add UI components:
a. src/components/ui/HistoryList.tsx – a simple component that receives an array of LedgerEntry objects and renders them chronologically (newest last) showing at, kind, and a JSON preview of data.

b. src/screens/ReceiptDetailScreen.tsx – existing receipt detail/edit screen should receive a navigation param "showHistory" or have a button "History" that navigates to this screen, loads the ledger entries filtered by recordId = receipt.id, and displays HistoryList. Ensure the screen still allows editing the receipt.
c. src/screens/MileageDetailScreen.tsx – analogous to receipt detail, with a History button and HistoryList filtered by mileage.id.

d. src/screens/SettingsScreen.tsx – add a new section showing ledger verification status: call ledger.verifyLedger(store) on mount; display "Verified • N entries • intact" when ok, otherwise display a warning with the first bad seq and reason.

7. Update ui_flow.json: add steps for opening a receipt’s History view from the receipt edit screen and for the Settings screen to display the ledger status text. Ensure the primary flow (edit receipt → open History → see correction) is represented.
8. Add unit tests (will be added later by the test writer) for:
- canonical JSON ordering and hash generation.
- verifyLedger detecting a changed field, missing entry, reordered entry, and changed prevHash, reporting firstBadSeq.
- corrections keep original entry and add corrected entry.
- import runs only once on a fresh install.
- CSV export appends verification line and ledger entry; tampering the file makes verification fail.
- PDF export verification code matches ledger head hash; unknown codes are reported as not from this app.
- backup round‑trip keeps a verifying ledger; tampered backup is rejected.

9. Ensure all existing tests continue to pass: do not modify existing receipt/mileage store signatures beyond adding async calls to ledger; keep existing validation, encryption, and UI flow unchanged.
10. Run lint, TypeScript compile, and existing Jest tests to confirm no regressions.
